preheader: Alphabet's $500B market drop, Serval's $150M raise, and Zverev hits world No. 1.

lead.headline: Alphabet Loses $500 Billion as Wall Street Recoils at AI Costs
lead.body: Alphabet shares fell nearly 13% after the company reported quarterly earnings, wiping out roughly $500 billion in market value. The plunge comes as investors worry that heavy spending on AI infrastructure is outstripping near-term revenue gains in core search and ad businesses.
lead.why: For your business and investing classes, this selloff shows how markets judge corporate capital allocation. When tech companies spend heavily on new tech, investors demand clear timeline gains in return.

stories.headline: ServiceNow shares plunge 25% following a slower contract forecast
stories.body: Workflow software company ServiceNow saw its stock fall nearly 27% to around $112 per share. The drop followed a slower forecast for contract growth, marking one of its worst single-day declines since going public.
stories.why: If you analyze enterprise software companies for internships or investing, watching how slowing contract forecasts impact stock valuations gives you key context for valuation models.

stories.headline: Sandisk shares jump after fiscal Q1 earnings beat and 8-for-1 stock split
stories.body: Sandisk beat Wall Street estimates for its fiscal first quarter and issued strong guidance for fiscal Q2. The memory chip maker also announced an eight-for-one stock split.
stories.why: Tracking corporate actions like stock splits helps you understand how public companies attempt to improve liquidity and manage share prices for retail investors.

stories.headline: Amazon blocks Meta's Muse AI agent, calling shopping bots ineffective
stories.body: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy criticized AI shopping agents as ineffective during an analyst call. Amazon blocked Meta's new AI assistant Muse from accessing its online store to protect its retail ecosystem.
stories.why: Understanding how tech platforms guard their data moats is crucial if you plan to launch a consumer tech startup or consult on platform strategy.

stories.headline: Anthropic deploys background self-assessment safety checks inside Claude
stories.body: Anthropic rolled out a background feature that allows its Claude AI model to silently evaluate its own chats for potential misuse and flag them for human review. The low-cost monitor runs in the background to improve platform safety.
stories.why: As enterprise AI adoption grows, risk compliance and automated monitoring are becoming major business drivers for software startups and consulting firms.

stories.headline: Former McKinsey consultant details the trade-offs of switching to big tech
stories.body: An Indian Institute of Management graduate detailed her move from McKinsey to Google after three years in consulting. She noted that consulting offered broad client exposure and travel, while the tech role brought deeper industry focus and a routine.
stories.why: When comparing summer internship paths, hearing practical accounts of consulting travel versus industry tech roles can help shape your long-term career choices.

stories.headline: PwC report shows AI increases skill demands for entry-level white-collar roles
stories.body: A PwC analysis of 2.4 million entry-level jobs found that junior roles most exposed to AI are seven times more likely to require skills traditionally expected of senior employees. Employers increasingly seek leadership and advanced technical abilities from fresh graduates.
stories.why: Developing practical technical and leadership skills during your first year at Merage will help you stand out for competitive internship recruiting.

stories.headline: Orange County prosecutors agree to purge DNA database after lawsuit involving UCI professor
stories.body: The Orange County District Attorney's office agreed to expunge profiles from its DNA database to settle a lawsuit challenging its constitutionality. A UC Irvine criminology professor who challenged the program in a 2021 lawsuit called the decision an important step forward.

stories.headline: Alexander Zverev secures world No. 1 ranking after victory in Vienna
stories.body: Alexander Zverev defeated Tallon Griekspoor 6-4, 7-5 at the Vienna Open on Thursday to advance to the quarterfinals. The win guarantees he will overtake Jannik Sinner to become world No. 1 for the first time in next week's rankings.

term.name: Capital Expenditure (CapEx)
term.definition: Capital expenditure refers to the money a company spends to buy, maintain, or upgrade physical assets like data centers, buildings, and hardware. Today's market selloff shows how investors grow anxious when CapEx spending rises faster than immediate revenue.

serve.headline: Serval raises $150M at a $3B valuation to challenge ServiceNow
serve.body: Enterprise software startup Serval raised $150 million in a new funding round led by Sequoia, valuing the company at $3 billion. Serval explicitly targets industry leader ServiceNow with ads and tools built to replace legacy enterprise software.
